answers.U2-S1: Some trees like oaks and beeches hang on to their old dead leaves because they can't let go, while tidy trees like maples drop them neatly.
answers.U2-S2: To show that the writer was wrong, because the new bud actually forms under the old leaf, like the sumach where it sits under the stalk like a cap.
answers.U2-S3: A funny comparison that makes the trees sound like indecisive, lazy people who can't make up their minds.
answers.U2-S4: Letting go of old leaves takes energy, so a dead tree keeps its withered leaves, while healthy trees drop them easily.
answers.U2-S5: The beginning or start of something.
answers.U2-S6: He partly agrees things start early, but says the real start is even earlier, in late summer when new buds form on trees.
answers.U2-S7: Because they are fully formed and waiting, like eggs, to be hatched by the warmth of spring.
answers.U2-S8: Each season gets the next one ready, like a mother, since buds for next year form during this year.
answers.U2-S9: His own observations of nature, like cutting open hickory buds and looking at fallen leaves and skunk-cabbage.
answers.U2-S10: It sums up the main idea that nature always prepares for spring before winter, like closing up a house.
